independent.summary: The editor-403 test's "writes nothing" check asserts no entity titled 'Zephyr Line' exists, but that title is nowhere in the document under test (alice's export holds the seeded 'Example Character'/'Example World' plus 'Alice Only' — 'Zephyr Line' belongs to the unit-test fixture), so the assertion passes unconditionally and would still pass if the 403 gate were removed and the whole graph written into alice's workspace.

planIds validates only `refModel`/`refId` on group members and nothing on a group's `label` or a member's `label`/`notes`, so a hand-edited document with a non-string there (e.g. `relationshipGroups[0].label = {}`) passes every pre-write check, the EntityType/RelationshipType/Entity insertMany calls all succeed, and the RelationshipGroup insert then throws a CastError — a 500 that leaves a partially written graph which the emptiness rule refuses to let the owner retry, contradicting the module's documented "nothing is written until everything has been checked".

The emptiness check and the five inserts are a read-then-write with no transaction, lock or unique guard, so two imports issued concurrently (two tabs, a retried request, an MCP/script caller) both see an empty workspace and both write, doubling every entity, group and question — a state the endpoint otherwise exists to prevent and which can then only be cleared by hand.

grades.reason: The error path already does `res.json().catch(() => null)` and falls back to `Import failed (${code})`, and the success path consumes the server's own 201 JSON, so the described failure does not exist.

The version is logged: `refusal('UNSUPPORTED_VERSION', ...)` interpolates the document's version into the reason that `importWorkspace`'s `fail()` logs at the light tier, and the quoted 'the body is not JSON' line belongs only to the malformed-JSON parser branch.

The dedicated 409 test (import.test.js:236-249) reads the entity list before and after and asserts the ids are identical; only the trivial "second import" case omits it, and that workspace was just legitimately populated by the previous test.

graphImporter.test.js's 'a seeded type registry does not make a workspace non-empty' test seeds `worlds` against the document's `Worlds`, asserts `skipped.entityTypes === 2`, that only one type row remains, and that categories were rewritten to the registry's casing.

triageGrades.reason: The new mount adds requireAuth + resolveWorkspace and the route adds requireWorkspaceRole('owner'), so authn/authz is genuinely touched.
No credentials, tokens or secret material is read, stored or logged by the change.
Nothing in the change touches billing, budgets or the AI cost path.
The import only inserts, and the 409 emptiness rule exists precisely so nothing existing is deleted or overwritten; the cited graphImporter.js:10 is a doc comment, not a destructive operation.
The change calls no third-party service — the only HTTP involved is the app's own /import endpoint.
No version bump, CI, deploy or migration change; the new IMPORT_* knobs are optional env overrides documented in docs/api.md.

summary: All four local findings are false positives — each describes a check or log line the diff already contains — and the review missed the vacuous assertion in the editor-403 test and the unvalidated group label/notes fields that can leave a half-written workspace.
